topic: Quantum contextuality and finite symplectic geometry
title: A degree-12 counterexample to Saniga et al.'s Section 4.4 line-subgeometry conjecture

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: We refute the line-subgeometry conjecture in Section 4.4, p. 20 of Saniga et al., Hexagons govern three-qubit contextuality, arXiv:2312.07738v3 (Quantum 9 (2025), 1601). The 75-line geometry contained in any three-qubit perp hyperplane has contextuality degree 12 but meets every classically embedded split Cayley hexagon in 15 lines. A 19-line configuration has degree 1 and intersection at least 3. Linear sections and signed Clifford transport prove that every perp in n >= 2 qubits has four times the degree of the full (n-1)-qubit line geometry; every four-qubit perp consequently has degree 252.
summary: Written proofs establish exact degree 12, exact three-regular-family intersection 15, the arbitrary-pole lifting identity, optimal-assignment characterization, and a 19-line witness. Degree is pole-independent, while canonical negative-line counts include 12 at IIZ and 24 at YYY. The pinned Lean declaration refutes the universal equality using the fixed IIZ witness; independent finite checks cover Pauli signs, the two-qubit minimum, all 63 negative-line counts, and the displayed configurations.
